# opencpn

**Marine chart plotter -- your position and AIS ships on nautical charts**

- **Version recorded:** 5.10.2
- **Categories:** `navigation-maps`, `ships`
- **Upstream:** <https://opencpn.org/>

## What it does

A chart plotter and navigation program for boats: it draws official nautical charts (vector S-57 ENCs and raster BSB/KAP charts, among others), shows your own position, heading and track from a GPS, plans routes with waypoints, and shows AIS ship targets with their names, courses and closest-approach warnings. The packaged build includes a chart downloader, a dashboard of instruments, a GRIB weather-file viewer and the world magnetic model.

## Why you would want it

It is the one program that makes the `ships` category more than a decoder: `rtl-ais` and `ais-catcher` turn an SDR into an AIS receiver that outputs NMEA, and OpenCPN is what draws those ships on a chart around you. For a station on or near the water -- a harbour event, a maritime-mobile operator, an EMCOMM deployment on the coast -- it is the offline alternative to web AIS maps and to phone apps. It is the open-source alternative to commercial PC chart plotters.

## Before it will work

Charts: none come with it beyond the world basemap. The bundled chart downloader fetches free official charts (for US waters, NOAA's ENCs) while online; after that they are files on the disk. A position source: OpenCPN's Connections settings take NMEA from a serial port or from the network, and gpsd as a network source. On this station that is gpsd itself, or the `gps-tether` launcher from the `navigation` profile, which serves gpsd's position as NMEA on 127.0.0.1 port 10110 (TCP). Ships: an AIS decoder (`rtl-ais`, `ais-catcher`) sending NMEA to a network port OpenCPN is told to listen on. None of these connections has been set up and tried by this project.

## How it installs

- apt: `opencpn`

## Known problems

Unmeasured here: OpenCPN has not been opened on any target, so its OpenGL display on the field laptop's Intel Iris Xe, its gpsd and `gps-tether` connections and an AIS feed from `rtl-ais` or `ais-catcher` are all untried; the paths above are what the programs document, not what has been run. The archives differ by three feature releases (5.8.4 to 5.14.1, measured 2026-09-30), so dialog names move between targets. OpenCPN's plugin manager can fetch further plugins from upstream's online catalog: those are binaries from outside apt, not reviewed or tracked by Hammunition, and `hammunition uninstall` does not remove them.
